original_value: Learning to classify unseen class samples at test time is popularly referred to as zero-shot learning (ZSL). If test samples can be from training (seen) as well as unseen classes, it is a more challenging problem due to the existence of strong bias towards seen classes. This problem is generally known as generalized zero-shot learning (GZSL). Thanks to the recent advances in generative models such as VAEs and GANs, sample synthesis based approaches have gained considerable attention for solving this problem. These approaches are able to handle the problem of class bias by synthesizing unseen class samples. However, these ZSL/GZSL models suffer due to the following key limitations: (i) Their training stage learns a class-conditioned generator using only seen class data and the training stage does not explicitly learn to generate the unseen class samples; (ii) They do not learn a generic optimal parameter which can easily generalize for both seen and unseen class generation; and (iii) If we only have access to a very few samples per seen class, these models tend to perform poorly. In this paper, we propose a meta-learning based generative model that naturally handles these limitations. The proposed model is based on integrating model-agnostic meta learning with a Wasserstein GAN (WGAN) to handle (i) and (iii), and uses a novel task distribution to handle (ii). Our proposed model yields significant improvements on standard ZSL as well as more challenging GZSL setting. In ZSL setting, our model yields 4.5%, 6.0%, 9.8%, and 27.9% relative improvements over the current state-of-the-art on CUB, AWA1, AWA2, and aPY datasets, respectively.

result.paraphrase: Learning to identify unseen-class samples at test time is commonly called zero-shot learning (ZSL). When test samples may come from both seen training classes and unseen classes, the task becomes harder because of a strong bias toward seen classes; this is known as generalized zero-shot learning (GZSL). Recent progress in generative models such as VAEs and GANs has made sample-synthesis methods attractive for addressing this issue, since they can reduce class bias by generating unseen-class samples. However, existing ZSL/GZSL models have three major limitations: (i) during training, they learn a class-conditioned generator only from seen-class data and do not explicitly learn to generate unseen-class samples; (ii) they fail to learn a generic optimal parameter that generalizes well to both seen- and unseen-class generation; and (iii) they perform poorly when only a very small number of samples is available per seen class. In this paper, we present a meta-learning-based generative model that naturally addresses these limitations. The proposed method combines model-agnostic meta learning with a Wasserstein GAN (WGAN) to handle (i) and (iii), and introduces a novel task distribution to handle (ii). Our model delivers substantial gains in both standard ZSL and the more difficult GZSL setting. In the ZSL setting, it achieves relative improvements of 4.5%, 6.0%, 9.8%, and 27.9% over the current state of the art on the CUB, AWA1, AWA2, and aPY datasets, respectively.
